The attractiveness and development of 
Bordeaux and its surrounding area have 
resulted in a tense property market for 
several years, with strong demand for 
student housing. To stack all the odds 
in your favour, here are some tips and 
advice to help you in your search for 
housing.

! Tips
>  Plan your search for housing before 
the school year starts to avoid any 
difficulties
>  Define your budget for the 1st month 
and the rest of the year
>  Get your rental application ready when 
you plan a visit (photocopy of your 
identity card, student card or school 
certificate, proof of residency not older 
than 3 months, bank details and the 
documents required for the guarantor)
>  Beware of dishonest advertisers, in 
particular some housing renters: do not 
make any reservation payments before 
visiting the accommodation, nor before 
signing the lease or being certain of 
the authenticity of the housing
>  Never pay in cash (or postal money 
order, Paypal, Western Union, pre-paid 
cards payments) and do not pay any 
rent or deposit until you have signed 
the lease
>  Do not go through list brokers who 
offer a list of housings in exchange for 
money
>  Always ask for proof of paid rent or a 
receipt after each payment is made
Housing solutions 
  Housing in CROUS university 
residences
The CROUS de Bordeaux-Aquitaine is the 
regional centre for university and school 
works in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region. Its 
ambition is to provide support to students 
during the key moments of their university 
life: information, reception and orientation, 
social aid, temporary job search, cultural 
activities, welcoming international students, 
social criteria grants, housing, catering, etc.
The structure offers housing in either 
traditional or recent university residences. 
In the recent residences, the rent depends 
on the type of housing and number of 
rooms (T1, T1 bis, T3 and T5). It is primarily 
intended for students with scholarships and 
international students enrolled in master’s 
or doctoral programmes.
Among the international students, those 
on individual mobility and enrolled in 
a master’s or doctoral programme in a 
higher education institution in Nouvelle 
Aquitaine have priority for CROUS housing. 
International students participating 
in Erasmus, BCI or other exchange 
programmes are also eligible for a CROUS 
accommodation. 
In either situation, students must complete 
an International Student Housing 
application and fill out a Student Social 
Application (Dossier Social Etudiant – DSE) 
• messervices.etudiant.gouv.fr

Private housing and room rental
*
 Lokaviz is a platform managed by the 
CROUS which lists housing offers in 
CROUS residences as well as housing 
offers from private owners. 
• lokaviz.fr
*
 Dossier facile is the French 
government’s digital platform to help 
you fill in a secure application 
• https://www.dossierfacile.fr/ 
*
 Un Deux Toit is a regional platform that 
lists offers of low-cost rooms in private 
homes. It assists students in their 
search for housing and helps them 
benefit from financial aid. 
• operationundeuxtoit.fr 
  Other websites for housing offers: 
• leboncoin.fr: the largest website 
of free classified adverts in France, 
including rental or house sharing 
opportunities. 
• roomlala.com: platform that puts 
owners and tenants in touch with each 
other to rent a room in a private owner’s 
housing. 
• erasmusu.com: community platform 
for students participating in an 
exchange programme (Erasmus or 
other).
International exchange students will also 
receive an informative email from the 
International Relations Office explaining 
the steps to follow. If you are a student 
registered with Campus France and are 
studying in the Académie de Bordeaux, 
Campus France will book your housing and 
send you the contact details of your future 
residence or university residence by email. 
• crous-bordeaux.fr/logements/carte-des-
logement/ 
CROUS housing allows you to benefit from 
advantages and services included in the 
rent (a moderate rent including utilities 
and WIFI). Your housing is equipped 
and furnished, can be located near the 
campuses and gives you the right to 
benefits from the CAF (see “Financial aid”).
  Social housing 
You can benefit from housing managed 
by social landlords, provided that you 
meet certain allocation criteria, particularly 
in terms of income. Waiting periods can 
sometimes be long.
• Online application via demande-
logement-social.gouv.fr  
• Further information on the allowance 
criteria and the application process on 
Bordeaux Métropole website  
• Yellome residences of Action Logement: 
https://www.yellome.fr/

House-share 
Sharing a house allows you to live in a 
larger house while keeping your budget 
low. It is also a good way to settle into a 
new city and make friends quickly... as long 
as you get on well with your roommates!
*
 Coop’Coloc is a student roommate 
service provided by ACLEF. Social 
landlords entrust ACLEF with quality 
housing so that the association can rent 
them out as furnished shared housing 
to students, at lower prices than usual. 
To benefit from Coop’Coloc housing 
in Bordeaux, you just have to apply by 
filling in the form on the website. 
• coopcoloc.fr  
*
 Kolocations A Projets Solidaires (KAPS) 
- meaning shared housing with 
solidarity projects – offers shared 
housing for students in exchange for 
their participation in solidarity projects 
with local residents. They offer low-cost 
rooms in shared housing in Pessac, a 
few minutes away from the university 
campus, in Bordeaux and in Bègles. 
• rejoins.afev.org/kaps 
  Here are other websites to help you to 
find roommates: 
• logements.pourlesjeunes.com 
• jesuisunjeune.com 
• lokaviz.fr (for students) 
• leboncoin.fr  
• appartager.com  
• lacartedescolocs.fr 
!
The housing.u-bordeaux-
montaigne.fr platform
In order to help you in your search for 
housing, the University provides students 
and landlords with its online housing 
platform. 
In partnership with Studapart, this 
platform, exclusively reserved for students 
of Bordeaux Montaigne University, 
lists thousands of private housing from 
individuals, student residences and real 
estate agencies around the campus and in 
the surrounding areas of Bordeaux.
Access to the platform 
housing.u-bordeaux-montaigne.fr
You just need to create an account to 
access the offers, which is verified and 
updated in real time, in order to:  
•  Find housing
•  Find your housemate(s) and share 
housing
•  Find a sublease
•  Find a temporary room
Please note: if you do not have a 
guarantor living in France, Studapart can 
act as a guarantor for you for the whole 
duration of your lease (paying service).
To register:  
•  New students: with your personal 
email address + the activation code 
HOUSINGMONTAIGNE
•  Student already registered at Bordeaux 
Montaigne University: with your logins
If you have any questions, please contact 
booking@studapart.com

Residential housing
*
 Private student residences are located 
near campus and in the surrounding 
areas of Bordeaux (YouFirst, les 
Estudines, Studyo, Studéa, Odalys, 
Studélites...). 
They offer comfortable housing, some 
of them include additional services 
(laundry, concierge service, etc.) and 
therefore require a higher budget 
(400€ to 700 €/month). 
• You can consult the offers on 
housing.u-bordeaux-montaigne.fr 
*
 Habitat Jeunes de Gironde offers 
housing in their residences for students 
with some financial resources (grants 
or parents’ allowances), whether or not 
they are employed. 
• Here is a list of residences in Gironde: 
https://www.habitatjeunes.org/
departement/33/  
• Apply for housing here: hj33.org 
*
*
*
 Intergenerational housing
In exchange for a helping hand and 
occasional services with daily tasks, you 
are hosted by and share the home of an 
elderly person above the age of 60, with 
interesting rental conditions for students. 
You can benefit from the CAF’s housing 
subsidies.
*
 Vivre avec : la cohabitation 
intergénérationnelle has been offering 
intergenerational and solidarity-based 
house-share in Bordeaux since 2004. 
The young person does not replace 
the professional caregivers that visit 
the elderly person, but their presence 
reassures the senior citizen and/or their 
family in moments of loneliness. 
• logement-solidaire.org
  Here are other solutions for 
intergenerational housing:
• ensemble2generations.fr  
• homiz.eu 
• wesharewecare.eu
*
*
*

In order to help you pay the necessary 
security deposit at the time of signing 
your lease (1 month’s rent excluding rental 
charges), you may benefit from the Loca-
Pass Advance. It is an interest-free credit 
spread out over maximum 25 months or 
that covers the duration of the lease. 
• locapass.actionlogement.fr 
 Avance 1er loyer 
(1st Rent Advance) 
In order to help you settle in your new flat, 
the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region has created 
an advance going from 100€ to 400€, 
which is then repayable over the course of 
24 months. People aged 18 to 30 whose 
housing and place of study or training is 
located in the region may apply for the 1st 
Rent Advance. 
• avanceloyer.solihanouvelleaquitaine.fr 
Financial aid 
 Housing subsidies (APL and ALS) 
As a student, you may benefit from 
subsidies from the CAF – the French Family 
Allowance Fund (Caisse d’Allocations 
Familiales), even in university residences 
housing. Every start of the month for the 
following month, you may benefit from 
either the Personalized Housing Assistance 
(APL – Aide personnalisée au logement) 
or the Social Housing Assistance (ALS – 
Allocation de logement Sociale). 
You can apply online here: 
• caf.fr
 Loca-Pass advance 
 Temporary housing solutions
*
 Located near the Saint-Jean train 
station, Bordeaux Youth Hostel 
(Auberge de Jeunesse de Bordeaux) 
welcomes young people all year long. 
It offers a bed (in a bedroom or in a 
dormitory) cheaper than a hotel.  
However, the Hostel does not aim to 
accommodate people for long stays. 
• auberge-jeunesse-bordeaux.com
*
 Airbnb is a global, social paying 
platform, allowing people to book and 
rent housing belonging to individuals 
for a long or short period anywhere 
in the world. It’s a short-term housing 
solution. Prices are variable.
  Housing for students with 
disabilities
If you have a disability, you may contact the 
CROUS to apply for adapted housing. You 
will have to fill in a specific application. 
• crous-bordeaux.fr

Good deals and legal 
support 
 Étu Récup’, the campus recycling centre  
Located on campus, this association gives 
a second life to items and furniture they 
retrieve, by selling them back at low price 
in their shop. 
• eturecup.org 
 Envie Gironde  
A store which offers household electrical 
appliances at low prices, as well as a repair 
service. 
• gironde.envie.org 
 Atelier Remuménage  
This association offers solidarity and eco-
friendly moving services and assists you 
with the administrative procedures involved 
in moving.  
• atelier-remumenage.org 
 Visale guarantee (Garantie Visale) 
If your lessor (the owner) requires that you 
have a guarantor (garant in French, see 
lexicon below) you likely may benefit from 
the Visale guarantee. Action Logement can 
act as your guarantor, free of charges, to 
your future lessor for the entire duration 
of the lease, whether in private housing, 
private residences, the CROUS’ university 
residences, Habitat Jeunes residences, etc.  
• visale.fr 
AQAFI
AQAFI is an association that helps 
international students upon arrival 
and guides them through all kinds 
of procedures (including housing 
matters). AQAFI will maintain a 
service on campus at the beginning 
of the academic year.
• aqafi33@gmail.com
• http://aqafi.org 
!

Lexicon
Assurance habitation – Home insurance 
Comprehensive risk insurance (assurance 
multi-risque habitation in French) is 
mandatory for the tenant: it insures the 
housing against rental risks, fire, water 
damage, natural disasters, theft. When 
handing over the keys of the housing, you 
will be asked to show a home insurance 
certificate.
Bail / Contrat de location – Lease / Rental 
agreement  
A (written) agreement between the tenant 
and the lessor. It specifies the rights and 
obligations of both the tenant and the 
lessor, and provides information on the 
housing being rented.
Bailleur – Lessor  
The entity which provides the housing for 
rental. It can be a private owner, an estate 
agency, a social lessor, the CROUS, or a 
private student residence.
Charges locatives – Rental charges 
Collective expenses for services such as lift 
or shared areas maintenance, water and 
sometimes heating.
Caution / Dépôt de garantie – Deposit / 
Guarantee deposit  
An amount which is equal to a month’s rent 
(without rental charges). It must be payed 
to the owner/lessor during the incoming 
inventory of fixtures, and will be entirely 
payed back within a month after the end 
of the lease, provided there has been no 
damage done to the house.
 ADIL Gironde 
This association gives free legal advice to 
tenants in case issues occur (dispute with 
the lessor, issue regarding the housing, 
unpaid rent, etc.). 
• adil33.org 
 La clinique du droit  
Bordeaux University’s free service for legal 
support. 
• cliniquedudroit.fr 
**

In the event of damage, the lessor must 
return the guarantee deposit within a 2 
months’ notice, along with proof of the 
damage, such as invoices.
Etat des lieux entrée/sortie – Incoming/
Outgoing inventory of fixtures  
At the time of having the keys to the 
housing handed over, you will conduct an 
inventory of fixtures with the lessor. It is a 
very detailed description of the house. It 
is important to describe and record any 
visible damage and carefully keep this 
document until your departure from the 
housing.
Garant / Caution solidaire – Guarantor / 
Third-party guarantee  
A tierce party takes responsibility for the 
payment of the rent and rental charges in 
the event of an unpaid rent. The guarantor 
must be solvent, meaning they must 
have sufficient income to take on this 
responsibility.
Loyer – Rent 
The amount to be payed each month in 
order to live in the housing. Ask whether 
rental charges are included in this amount.
Préavis – Notice 
You can terminate your lease at any time, 
provided that you respect the notice 
period. This inquiry for termination must 
be done by sending the lessor a registered 
letter with acknowledgement of receipt 
(from a post office).
